Problem size\n    problem_size: Any,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    # Hardware constraints\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 4.5e8,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 1.0e6,\n    dofs_per_gb: float = 1.2e7,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.95\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Args:\n        problem_size (tuple): The 3D problem grid dimensions (e.g., Px, Py, Pz).\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured Figure of Merit (FOM) from the completed run.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum FOM (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 4.5e8).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant modeling communication overhead (default 1.0e6).\n        dofs_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (DOFs per GB of RAM, default 1.2e7).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.95).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"   \n    total_dofs = problem_size[0] * problem_size[1] * problem_size[2]\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero. Suggest using at least one task.\"}\n\n    # --- 2. Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    dofs_per_rank = total_dofs / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cpu_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n\n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(dofs_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_ranks * cpu_per_rank\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_dofs / dofs_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used)\n\n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"dofs_per_rank\": int(dofs_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n    # --- 3. Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---        \n    # Primary STOP condition: Performance is good enough.\n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    # Primary RETRY condition: Memory is the bottleneck.\n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The problem size is too large for the allocated memory. Suggest significantly reducing the problem size.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    # Secondary RETRY condition: Scaling is the bottleneck.\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the problem size per rank is too small. Suggest significantly increasing the problem size to provide more work per rank.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    # Tertiary RETRY condition: Cores are underutilized on a single node.\n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Suggest increasing the number of tasks to better utilize the hardware.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    # Default RETRY condition: Performance is simply not good enough yet.\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Suggest moderately increasing the problem size to improve the work-per-rank and move closer to the optimal FOM.\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }"

dockerfile
# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for building C/MPI applications
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation of packages
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, MPI, and certificates for the amg2023 application.
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library.
# We clean up apt cache afterwards to reduce image size, without using 'purge'.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized and cloud environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI traffic is routed over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disable shared-memory mechanisms that can be problematic within containers.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Clone the latest branch of the amg2023 (LLNL AMG) source code, build the executable,
# copy it to a system-wide location on the PATH, and clean up the source directory.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg2023 && \
    cd /tmp/amg2023/test && \
    make && \
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg2023

# Set a default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command to execute when the container starts.
# This will run the amg benchmark executable.
CMD ["amg"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for building C/MPI applications
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation of packages
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, MPI, and certificates for the amg2023 application.
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library.
# We clean up apt cache afterwards to reduce image size, without using 'purge'.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized and cloud environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI traffic is routed over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disable shared-memory mechanisms that can be problematic within containers.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Clone the latest branch of the amg2023 (LLNL AMG) source code, build the executable,
# copy it to a system-wide location on the PATH, and clean up the source directory.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg2023 && \
    cd /tmp/amg2023/test && \
    # FIX: Build dependent libraries ('make lib') before the main executable ('make amg')
    # to resolve linker errors where libraries like 'libparcsr_ls.a' could not be found.
    make lib && \
    make amg && \
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg2023

# Set a default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command to execute when the container starts.
# This will run the amg benchmark executable.
CMD ["amg"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for building C/MPI applications
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation of packages
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, MPI, and certificates for the amg2023 application.
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library.
# We clean up apt cache afterwards to reduce image size, without using 'purge'.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized and cloud environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI traffic is routed over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disable shared-memory mechanisms that can be problematic within containers.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Clone the latest branch of the amg2023 (LLNL AMG) source code, build the executable,
# copy it to a system-wide location on the PATH, and clean up the source directory.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg2023 && \
    # FIX: Correct the build directory to 'struct' where the main Makefile is located.
    cd /tmp/amg2023/struct && \
    # A single 'make' command here builds all libraries and the final executable.
    make && \
    # Copy the compiled binary from its correct output location to the system PATH.
    cp ../test/amg /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg2023

# Set a default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command to execute when the container starts.
# This will run the amg benchmark executable.
CMD ["amg"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for building C/MPI applications
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation of packages
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, MPI, and certificates for the amg2023 application.
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library.
# We clean up apt cache afterwards to reduce image size, without using 'purge'.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized and cloud environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI traffic is routed over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disable shared-memory mechanisms that can be problematic within containers.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Clone the latest branch of the amg2023 (LLNL AMG) source code, build the executable,
# copy it to a system-wide location on the PATH, and clean up the source directory.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg2023 && \
    # FIX: Follow the correct build procedure for AMG, which requires building the hypre library first.
    # Navigate to the hypre library source.
    cd /tmp/amg2023/hypre/src && \
    # Configure the hypre library, enabling MPI support which is essential for this application.
    ./configure --with-MPI && \
    # Compile the hypre library.
    make && \
    # Navigate to the test directory to build the amg executable itself.
    cd ../../test && \
    make && \
    # Copy the compiled binary to a location on the system PATH.
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Clean up the source directory to reduce image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg2023

# Set a default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command to execute when the container starts.
# This will run the amg benchmark executable.
CMD ["amg"]

Decision 2: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: The second attempt, which maximized task count and aggressively scaled the problem size, resulted in the same extremely low Figure of Merit (FOM). This strongly suggests the run failed, likely due to an Out-of-Memory (OOM) error or a timeout, as the calculated memory utilization was a critical 94%. The evaluation function confirms performance is near zero. The new strategy is to slightly reduce the problem size to a safer memory footprint (~85% utilization) to prevent a crash, while maintaining full node utilization (128 tasks) and high scaling efficiency.
